title_en: Krishnadas Is Shown the Path of Devotion
translation:
_Agalod gaamthi Krishnadas aavya ||_
_Bhakti mukti paami haide harakhaya ||1||_
(Krishnadas came from the village of Agalod; having attained bhakti (devotion) and liberation, his heart rejoiced.)

Krishnadas's mother's name was Tejbai and his father's name was Damodardas Dave. In Idar, Damodardas Dave was a well-known physician (vaidya) and astrologer. Krishnadas was born in Samvat 1700, on the second day of the bright half of Kartak. In Samvat 1710, Damodardas passed away (attained the heavenly abode). In Samvat 1712, when the Muslims conquered Idar, Krishnadas, together with his mother, lived in Hidovar and pursued his studies there. He used to perform intense meditation (mahadhyan) on Ganpati. When Ganpati told him to ask for a boon, he asked instead for devotion to Shri Hari. Ganpati told him that only a Sadguru can grant the gift of devotion — devotion becomes firm through the company of saints (satsang). Ganpati then brought him, in the Kanam region, to Puniyad, to Sadguru Jivanji Maharaj, who was in the form of Sarangpani. At the edge of the village of Puniyad, a conversation took place with Naranadas. His doubts were resolved right there, and when he asked Naranadas for initiation (diksha), Naranadas brought him to Sadguru Jivanji Maharaj. Removing Krishnadas's doubt and confusion, Sadguru Jivanji Maharaj gave him initiation, gave him his own rosary (mala), and told him to give up the ritualist worship of Omkar and to walk the path of the Rarankar exclusive devotion (ananya bhakti) and worship of the saints and devotees. Returning home from Puniyad to his native place, he came to Agalod, to the house of his host, the Kadva Kanbi Patel named Dhana. Because he had taken the vow of exclusive devotion from Sadguru Jivanji Maharaj, he would not accept cooked food or provisions directly.

Then Dhana asked that he too be taken under the Sadguru's pledge (banu). So Dhana, taking Mangala and Shitala with him, came to Puniyad and had them given kanthi-diksha (initiation with the neck-thread) by Sadguru Jivanji Maharaj, making them uda-bhakts, exclusive Vaishnavs. He attained the refuge of Hari (passed away) at his daughter's house in the village of Sabalpur. At the place of his samadhi (tomb-shrine) there is a tulsi enclosure (tulsi kyaro); his family seat is at present at Sardarpur, Taluka Vijapur, District Mehsana. Even today, as witness to this event, Ganpati is enshrined at the edge of Puniyad. (— From the Parchari of Krishnadas.)

Even a deity such as Ganpati cannot grant devotion to Vishnu. Only a saint, a Sadguru, can give this devotion. Therefore Ganpati, who brought about the meeting between Krishnadas and Sadguru Jivanji Maharaj, was the giver of riddhi-siddhi (worldly power and prosperity). Krishnadas did not accept the riddhi-siddhi that leads to hell. Thus there is no possibility that one who worships Ganpati will attain bhakti. Moreover, uda-bhakts do not worship any god or goddess that would lead us to a lower state (adhogati). Worshipping them cannot bring about our welfare — this principle is proved by this episode of Krishnadas.
